newsitem.title: USA: Abbott drugs segment grows fastest in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Abbott drugs segment grows fastest in Q3.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc said third-quarter sales growth in its pharmaceutical and nutritional products business segment outstripped that of its hospital and laboratory products segment.

The drugs and medical products giant on Tuesday reported worldwide sales of pharmaceutical and nutritional products were $1.45 billion in the third quarter, an 11.7 percent increase from $1.3 billion in the same period last year.
Of total sales in the segment, U.S. sales accounted for $957 million, and non-U.S. sales for $499 million.
Shares in Abbott were unchanged at 50-3/8.

Global sales of hospital and laboratory products were $1.19 billion on the quarter, up 9.4 percent from last year, Abbott said. U.S. sales comprised $648 million of that total, and non-U.S. sales were $542 million.

On a geographic basis, total Abbott sales in U.S. markets were $1.6 billion in the third quarter, up 13.4 percent from $1.41 billion a year ago. Total non-U.S. sales, including direct exports from the United States, grew to $1.04 billion, a 6.7 percent increase from $976 million a year ago.
Non-U.S. sales were reduced 6.5 percent due to the effect of the relatively stronger U.S. dollar, Abbott said.

In the first nine months of 1996, worldwide sales were $8.01 billion, up 8.1 percent from a year ago. Earnings per share for the same period increased 14.4 percent to $1.75 from $1.53 a year ago. Net earnings were $1.37 billion, up 12.1 percent from $1.22 billion for the first nine months of 1995.
Worldwide pharmaceutical and nutritional products sales were $4.58 billion in the first nine months, a 9.9 percent increase from $4.17 billion a year earlier, Abbott said.
Worldwide sales of hospital and laboratory products totaled $3.43 billion in the first nine months, up 5.8 percent from $3.243 billion one year ago, the company said.

"Abbott's worldwide pharmaceutical business, along with our entrance into the glucose monitoring and diagnostic imaging markets, drove the company's strong performance this quarter," said chief executive and chairman Duane Burnham.
During the third quarter, investment in research and development rose to $279 million, up nine percent from the same period in 1995, Abbott said.
